audit_findings.title: Finance-lease principal may escape owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 finance-lease principal payments of $3.825m, equal to 9.8% of the $39.2m anchor; if omitted and recurring, approximately $53.7m or $2.28 per share of base value
audit_findings.mechanism: OE may add back finance-lease asset depreciation while failing to deduct the corresponding principal cash payments; treating the liability as context-only debt does not correct an OE omission
audit_findings.evidence: The Company does not record single lease expense for the rental payments under finance leases, but rather payments under the finance lease obligations are recognized as a reduction of the finance lease obligation and as interest expense over the remaining term of the lease.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that finance leases generated $4.353m of FY2025 depreciation and $3.825m of principal payments. They do not demonstrate whether the historical OE calculations deducted that principal or otherwise charged an equivalent economic lease cost. The potential error is large enough to alter the bear, base and bull values, so it remains material but unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every OE year to finance-lease depreciation, principal payments and non-cash lease-asset additions; rerun all scenarios after applying one consistent economic-cost treatment without double counting.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized SaaS spending may be missing from capex
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 gross capitalized SaaS implementation costs increased by $4.979m, equal to 12.7% of the $39.2m anchor; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Capitalized SaaS cash spending runs through operating cash flow and other assets, so an OE calculation deducting only investing-section property and intangible purchases can omit it
audit_findings.evidence: The decrease in cash provided by operating activities was due to a decrease in cash provided by operating assets and liabilities, primarily attributable to the timing of accounts payable payments and merchandise inventory purchases, and higher capitalized SaaS implementation costs, partially offset by an increase in cash provided by net income as adjusted for non-cash items.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a $4.979m increase in gross SaaS implementation costs during FY2025, including $0.7m of capitalized internal compensation, but the supplied record does not establish whether OE captured those amounts. An omission of this scale could materially inflate the anchor and projected OE, although its recurring level is not established.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile annual OE capex to the SaaS asset roll-forward and operating-cash-flow changes, including capitalized internal labor; rerun the trend anchor and scenarios for any omitted cash investment.

audit_findings.title: Forecast may omit the announced capex step-up
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2026 computed capex range of $44.636m-$49.636m based on $39.936m spent through nine months plus $4.7m-$9.7m planned for the remainder, or $13.435m-$18.435m above FY2025
audit_findings.mechanism: Forecast OE and growth are overstated if store-driven cash flows are projected without deducting the related reinvestment from forecast equity cash flow
audit_findings.evidence: We plan to spend approximately $50.0 million to $55.0 million on capital expenditures during fiscal year 2026 primarily in connection with expected new store openings and store relocations/remodels.
audit_findings.explanation: The step-up is no longer merely announced: nine-month FY2026 property-and-equipment spending already reached $39.936m. The valuation record does not show an explicit forecast charge for this investment. Not all spending is necessarily maintenance capex, but growth capex cannot be ignored while its resulting growth is credited; the scale is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Separate FY2026 spending into maintenance, replacement and growth components; map growth capex to incremental store cash flows and timing, then rerun the DCF with explicit annual reinvestment.

audit_findings.title: Supplier concentration could break the growth and margin assumptions
audit_findings.mechanism: A UNFI disruption or repricing would reduce sales availability, gross margin and working-capital efficiency, lowering OE and achievable growth
audit_findings.evidence: UNFI is our single largest third-party supplier, accounting for approximately 69% of our total purchases in fiscal year 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The 69% purchase concentration and the FY2025 cybersecurity disruption demonstrate exposure, but they do not establish a presently omitted loss or a sustainable margin adjustment. The $2.0m FY2026 insurance recovery is not a measure of the underlying recurring downside. This is therefore a forward-looking risk to monitor rather than a demonstrated valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Run outage, contract-repricing and alternative-distribution stresses using documented lost sales, uninsured costs, margin changes and working-capital requirements; revisit before the September 2028 UNFI renewal decision.

audit_findings.title: A nonrecurring CFO-transition charge remains in the anchor history
audit_findings.magnitude: $0.5m in FY2025 and $0.4m in FY2024; a full recurring $0.5m anchor adjustment would add approximately $7.0m or $0.30 per share to base value
audit_findings.mechanism: Retaining transition-specific SBC reduces historical OE and therefore can slightly depress the log-trend anchor
audit_findings.evidence: During the years ended September 30, 2025 and 2024, the Company accelerated the vesting of certain restricted stock units upon the retirement of the Company’s former Chief Financial Officer and for two grantees, making them fully vested, resulting in incremental share-based compensation expense of $ 0.5 million and $ 0.4 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The FY2025 charge equals only 1.3% of the $39.2m anchor. Even treating the entire $0.5m as a recurring anchor adjustment would increase base value by about $0.30 per share, far below the $3.87 gap between the $24.06 base value and the $27.93 market price and the $11.09 gap to the $16.84 buy-below price. It therefore does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Document the deliberate conservative retention of the $0.5m and $0.4m transition charges; no valuation rerun is required unless other nonrecurring compensation items are identified.
